result.title: Toward Planning Representations That Separate Task Structure from Visual Content
result.summary: Effective planning requires representations that preserve task-relevant geometry and object identity while ignoring visual variation that does not alter the task. Existing evaluations of visual generalization often change several factors simultaneously, making the source of a failure difficult to identify. We introduce a controlled evaluation of object-goal navigation (ObjectNav), the task of reaching an instance of a named object category, in procedurally generated ProcTHOR houses. Training and evaluation houses share floor plans, object locations, goals, and start states, while visual factors are changed individually or in combination. Across model-free reinforcement learning (RL), model-based RL, and agents using frozen pretrained visual representations, our results show that appearance changes impair navigation, but their effects differ sharply by factor. Surface material changes account for most of the average change in success, whereas clutter and lighting have little effect. The magnitude of a global image statistics shift does not reliably predict performance: changing only the goal object's appearance can substantially impair an end-to-end agent despite a small image-level change. We found that a model based agent that plans over frozen features from the pretrained DINOv2 image encoder achieves the highest success (0.83) under the full shift, but remains sensitive to surface appearance. Our experiments reveal an important requirement for planning representations: they must separate invariant spatial task structure from appearance.

AI.brief_summary: 在程序生成的 ProcTHOR 房屋中构建受控 ObjectNav 评测：固定布局、目标与起点，单独或组合改变视觉因素，比较无模型 RL、基于模型 RL 与冻结预训练视觉特征智能体。结果显示表面材质变化影响最大，全局图像统计偏移无法预测性能，规划表示需分离任务空间结构与外观。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作以因子隔离方式诊断外观扰动造成的表示失败，与 LVR 关注的视觉细节保留、视觉旁路与信息坍缩直接相关；其冻结 DINOv2 特征上的基于模型规划结果，可供核查「哪些视觉信息应进入 latent 状态、哪些应被剥离」。
